h1: The 8 Best One-Touch Microwaves of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 one-touch microwaves scored on presets, power, safety features, evenness and value, from Chefman to Toshiba sensor.
summary: The Chefman 1.1 is the best one-touch microwave, with six presets, mute, eco mode and a child lock. The Toshiba 1.2 adds humidity sensor cooking, the BLACK+DECKER is the roomy preset pick, and the COMFEE' is the quiet compact choice for dorms.
intro: A microwave should be the easiest appliance in your kitchen, and yet many are cluttered with menus nobody uses. What most people want is simple: press one button, get a good result and not be startled by beeps at midnight. The details that make that possible are often missing from the spec sheet.

This ranking covers eight countertop microwaves from 0.7 to 1.2 cubic feet. We reviewed their listings for named presets, wattage, child lock, mute and defrost features, since those are published, and we ranked each on how simply it works day to day.

Typical owner complaints include 700W ovens that need long cook times, keypads with too many keys, beeps that cannot be silenced, and door latches that are fiddly. Each pick below is scored against those problems, with the tradeoff stated plainly.

products.name: Chefman 1.1 Cu. Ft. Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A 1000W Chefman with six one-touch presets, memory keys, eco mode, child lock and a mute button.
products.description:
The Chefman 1.1 cubic foot microwave pairs 1000W with ten power levels and six one-touch presets that include popcorn, pizza and leftovers. A +30 second key adds time in a press, and a memory function stores a favorite routine. Eco mode turns off the display when idle, the Audio key silences the beeps, and the child lock works two ways: a latch on the handle and a Lock Mode for the keypad. The listed footprint is about 20 inches wide.

It tops the ranking because it is the only model that stacks everything this guide is about: named presets, a shortcut for extra time, a silencer and a lock, in a mid-size body at the $50 to $100 bucket. A 1.1 cubic foot cavity takes a standard dinner plate, and 1000W is the wattage most recipe times assume. The tradeoff is that there is no sensor cooking, so you still guess times for odd foods. Against the Toshiba, you lose the humidity sensor but pay far less.

Buy it for a family kitchen, a shared apartment where midnight beeps matter or a first home. Skip it if you want sensor cooking or a stainless finish, which the listing does not offer.
products.idealFor: Families and shared homes who want simple, quiet, preset-driven use.
products.skipIf: You want sensor cooking or a stainless finish.

products.name: TOSHIBA 1.2 Cu. Ft. 1000W Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A 1.2 cubic foot, 1000W Toshiba with a humidity sensor, auto menus, mute and one-touch 1 to 6 minute start.
products.description:
The Toshiba is a 1.2 cubic foot oven with 1000W output and a listed input of 1600W, a 12.4 inch glass turntable and external dimensions of about 20.6 by 14.6 by 11.8 inches. A humidity sensor adjusts time and power for sensor reheat, six preset menus cover foods such as pizza and vegetables, and ten power levels, a clock and a kitchen timer sit alongside. One-touch start runs 1 to 6 minutes at full power, defrost works by weight or time and a mute function silences the beeps.

It ranks second because the humidity sensor is the one real cooking advantage here: it watches steam coming off the food and stops, which prevents the classic rubbery, over-reheated leftover. It costs more, in the $100 to $200 bucket, than the Chefman, and the keypad shows more menu keys than a purely one-touch buyer needs. The 1.2 cubic foot cavity and 12.4 inch turntable also fit a large plate or a bowl better than the 0.7 cubic foot models.

Buy it if you reheat varied foods and want the oven to judge the time. Skip it if you prefer a plain keypad and the lower price.
products.idealFor: Cooks who reheat varied foods and want sensor timing.
products.skipIf: You want the lowest price or a bare keypad.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 1.1 Cu. Ft. Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A 1000W, 1.1 cubic foot oven with six one-touch presets and a fingerprint-resistant black finish.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER lists 1.1 cubic feet, 1000W and ten power levels, with six one-touch programs for popcorn, potato, pizza, frozen vegetable, beverage and dinner plate. Express cooking shortcut keys start heating instantly, and the child lock engages by holding the cancel button for 5 seconds. The finish is described as fingerprint resistant, and the maker says the cavity takes standard dinner plates.

It ranks third because the preset list is as practical as the Chefman's, and a dedicated dinner plate preset is a thoughtful touch, but the listing names no mute function and no eco mode. That leaves it behind the Chefman 1.1 for a household that cares about silence or standby draw. It lists in the same bucket as the leader, $50 to $100.

Buy it for a roomy cavity and clear presets if beeps are not a concern. Skip it if you want a mute key.
products.idealFor: Households that want a roomy oven with clear presets.
products.skipIf: You need a mute option for night use.

products.name: Chefman 0.9 Cu. Ft. Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A 900W Chefman with six one-touch presets, memory, eco mode, child lock and mute.
products.description:
The Chefman 0.9 cubic foot microwave is rated 900W with ten power levels and six one-touch Express Cook presets, the same set as its larger sibling. The +30 second key, a memory function, an eco mode that shuts off the display, a handle child lock with a keypad Lock Mode and a mute Audio key all appear in the listing. The size is listed at roughly 18.9 inches wide.

It ranks fourth because it carries the same feature set as the 1.1 cubic foot model in a smaller, lower-power body, and 900W adds a bit to cook times against the 1000W recipes most packages print. The cavity sits between the compact and full-size classes, so it suits two people better than a family. Price band is $50 to $100.

Buy it for a small kitchen that still wants the full list of one-touch features. Skip it if you routinely heat large plates, where the 1.1 is easier.
pros: Child lock on handle and keypad
products.idealFor: Couples and small kitchens that still want presets and quiet.
products.skipIf: You heat large plates or cook for several people.

products.name: COMFEE' 0.7 Cu. Ft. Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A 700W compact with one-touch 1 to 6 minute keys, six auto menus, two defrost modes, mute and a two-step child lock.
products.description:
The COMFEE' lists 0.7 cubic feet and 700W, with one-touch express cooking for 1 to 6 minutes, a +30 second key and six auto-cook menus: popcorn, potato, pizza, frozen vegetable, beverage and reheat. Defrost works by weight or by time. A mute function turns beeps off by holding the sound key for 3 seconds, ECO mode is listed as cutting standby power by 50 percent, and a two-step child lock is built in. The listed footprint is about 17.3 by 10.2 by 12.7 inches.

It ranks fifth because the feature list is complete for a compact oven, with both mute and lock, but the 700W rating means longer heating times and the cavity is tight for dinner plates. It beats the 0.7 Chefman on the explicit defrost modes and the 50 percent standby claim, and the price band is $50 to $100.

Buy it for a dorm, office or one-person kitchen. Skip it if you cook for several people.

products.name: Chefman 0.7 Cu. Ft. Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A 700W compact with six one-touch presets, ten power levels, mute and a handle child lock.
products.description:
The Chefman 0.7 cubic foot oven lists 700W with ten power levels and six one-touch presets, the same set as the 0.9 above it, plus a +30 second key. A handle child lock requires you to pull up on the top edge to open, and the Audio key mutes the beeps. The black exterior wipes clean and the glass turntable is listed as top-rack dishwasher safe. Listed width is about 17.5 inches.

It ranks sixth because the presets and mute are good, but it drops the memory function and eco mode of the larger Chefman models, and 700W makes cooking slow. Against the COMFEE', it offers a more complete preset list and simpler styling. Price band is $50 to $100.

Buy it for small counters where a quiet, preset-driven oven is the goal. Skip it if you need to heat full plates.
products.idealFor: People who want a quiet preset-driven microwave for a small counter.

products.name: GE 0.7 Cu. Ft. Countertop Microwave GCST07N1WSS
products.verdict: A stainless 700W GE with one-touch express cooking, four convenience settings, auto defrost and child lock.
products.description:
The GE GCST07N1WSS is a 0.7 cubic foot, 700W stainless steel microwave listed at about 17.3 inches wide, 12.75 deep and 10.2 high. It offers one-touch express cooking, four convenience cook settings, both manual and auto defrost, a digital display and a child lock you can disable when not needed. The listing asks for 3 inches of clearance at each side and above, 1 inch behind and an unobstructed bottom for airflow.

It ranks seventh because it sits in the $100 to $200 bucket for a 700W compact with fewer named presets than the Chefman and COMFEE' models, and the listing does not mention a mute key. The brand and stainless finish are the draw, plus auto defrost that adjusts time and power to prevent overcooked edges. The clearance note matters: do not wedge it into a tight shelf.

Buy it if you want a GE label and a stainless look in a compact size. Skip it if value or silence is the priority.

keySpecs.label: Clearance
keySpecs.value: 3 in sides and top, 1 in rear

products.idealFor: Buyers who want a known brand in a compact stainless body.
products.skipIf: You want the best value or a mute key.

products.name: Chefman Compact Countertop Microwave 0.7 Cu Ft Stainless
products.verdict: A stainless 700W Chefman with three one-touch presets, +30 second key, mute, handle child lock and a one-year assurance.
products.description:
This Chefman compact is a stainless 0.7 cubic foot, 700W microwave with ten power levels and three one-touch presets: popcorn, beverages and leftovers. A +30 second key, time and weight defrost, a Sound key that mutes beeps and a handle child lock are listed. It is cETL approved and carries a 1-year assurance from Chefman, with model code RJ55-SS-7-V2.

It ranks last because it has the fewest presets of the Chefman family and no memory function or eco mode in the listing. It does give a stainless look at the $50 to $100 bucket, plus a stated assurance period that the black models do not mention. Against the GE compact, it carries more one-touch features for the price.

Buy it if you want stainless on a small counter and basic presets. Skip it if you want a wider preset list.
products.idealFor: Small-counter buyers who want stainless and basic one-touch use.
products.skipIf: You want a long preset list.

methodology.title: One-touch operation
methodology.description: We read how many named presets each microwave lists, whether it has a +30 second or 1 to 6 minute shortcut and how many steps sit between a press and heat.

methodology.title: Power and capacity
methodology.description: We compared wattage from 700W to 1000W and cavity sizes from 0.7 to 1.2 cubic feet against plate size and household size.

methodology.title: Noise and safety
methodology.description: We weighed mute keys, handle latches, keypad locks and eco modes, since shared homes care about quiet and children.

methodology.title: Defrost and sensing
methodology.description: We looked for weight and time defrost, auto modes and the humidity sensor that only the Toshiba lists.

methodology.title: Value for the bucket
methodology.description: We set feature depth against the $50 to $100 and $100 to $200 buckets, rewarding stated features over brand alone.

whatMatters.detail: A preset key runs a stored time and power for a food, and the useful ones are popcorn, beverage, leftovers and potato. A +30 second key and 1 to 6 minute one-touch start cover everything else. Count the named presets in the listing, and look at the photos of the keypad, since a preset list that reads well can sit on a cluttered panel.

Most recipe times assume 1000W, so a 700W oven needs roughly 40 percent longer for the same job and a 900W oven needs about 10 percent. Cavity size matters for plates: a 0.7 cubic foot interior is tight for a 10 inch dinner plate, while 1.1 and 1.2 cubic feet fit one. Compare the listed turntable size, such as 12.4 inches on the Toshiba, to your plates.

Beeps are the most common complaint in shared homes, and a mute key silences them without muting the cooking. Eco mode turns off the display when idle, and COMFEE' claims a 50 percent standby saving. Check the listing for the words mute, sound on/off or audio, and how you toggle it, since some require a three-second hold.

Two designs exist: a handle latch that stops the door from opening and a keypad lock that stops cooking from starting. The Chefman models list both, while the BLACK+DECKER uses a five-second cancel-button hold. Read how it engages and releases before you buy, and test it once during setup so you can undo it quickly when you need to.

Defrost by weight asks you to enter the food's weight, and by time lets you set minutes. Auto defrost adjusts power in steps to avoid cooked edges, and a humidity sensor stops cooking when steam rises. Look for which of these the listing names. If you thaw meat often, pick a model with weight-based defrost, such as the COMFEE', Toshiba or Chefman stainless.

cards.label: Presets
cards.text: Run a fixed time and power, which works when the food matches what the key assumes. They are cheap and predictable, but a big or small portion can come out wrong. Picks: Chefman 1.1, BLACK+DECKER, Chefman 0.9 and the compact models.

cards.label: Sensor
cards.text: Watches steam and stops when the food is done, which adapts to portion size and starting temperature. It costs more and has more menu keys. Pick: Toshiba 1.2.

howToChoose.note: Default to presets, and pay for sensor cooking only if you reheat varied foods daily.

cards.text: Large, clearly labeled preset keys, a bright readout, a mute option and few steps between pressing a button and the oven starting. A 1 to 6 minute one-touch start is simpler than typing times.

faq.q: What does one-touch mean on a microwave?
faq.a: It means a key that starts a stored cooking routine, such as popcorn, or runs a preset time such as 1 minute at full power. Listings vary in how many presets they name, so count them and look at the keypad photos. A +30 second key is a handy shortcut on all the Chefman models.

faq.q: What is the most common microwave buying mistake?
faq.a: Choosing the smallest model for the lowest price, then finding that a dinner plate will not turn. Measure your plates and compare them with the cavity and turntable size before you order. The second mistake is ignoring wattage, since 700W models need much longer than recipes assume.

faq.q: Is the Toshiba worth it over the Chefman 1.1?
faq.a: If you reheat varied foods and want a humidity sensor to judge time, yes. For coffee, popcorn and leftovers, the Chefman delivers presets, mute and lock at a lower price. The Toshiba also gives a 12.4 inch turntable.

faq.q: How do I use the child lock?
faq.a: On Chefman models, the handle latch engages when you close the door and the keypad Lock Mode disables the control panel. The BLACK+DECKER locks by holding cancel for 5 seconds. Check the manual for the unlock step so you are not stuck.

faq.q: How do I keep a microwave clean?
faq.a: Steam a bowl of water with lemon or vinegar for a few minutes, let it sit, then wipe the interior. Remove and wash the turntable, which is top-rack dishwasher safe on the Chefman 0.7. Cover foods that spatter.

faq.q: Can I use a microwave with an extension cord?
faq.a: It is not recommended, since microwaves draw a lot of current. Plug them directly into a wall outlet. Also leave the clearance the maker lists: the GE asks for 3 inches at each side and above, and 1 inch at the back.

finalTake: The Chefman 1.1 is the best microwave for simple, quiet, everyday use, thanks to six presets, a mute key and two kinds of child lock at a mid-range price. Pick the Toshiba if you want sensor cooking, the BLACK+DECKER for a roomy cavity and the COMFEE' for a dorm. Because listings rarely show every key, check the keypad in photos before you order.
